opportunities.title: Cities Deliver: AI Solutions for Public Services (Rockefeller Foundation + OpenAI Foundation global open call, US$50M)
opportunities.funder: The Rockefeller Foundation and OpenAI Foundation
opportunities.program: Cities Deliver: AI Solutions for Public Services
opportunities.deadline_text: November 29, 2026 - Screening and Round 1 Proposal due at 11:59pm EST; Round 2 proposals due March 1, 2027 at 11:59pm U.S. Eastern Time.
opportunities.funding_text: Seed track: $500,000 to <$1 million (early concepts ready for a first city pilot); Scale track: $1 to $2 million (already piloted). Total commitment $50 million. 50% disbursed at the start and 50% upon a documented mid-term milestone.
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Nonprofit organizations (including university departments/labs and fiscally sponsored organizations); public benefit corporations and, in limited circumstances, for-profits. Governments cannot apply directly. Every applicant must have a city government partner (letter of intent at Round 1; official letter/MOU at Round 2). Individuals excluded.
opportunities.eligible_countries: Global: cities in Sub-Saharan Africa, MENA, Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean, Europe, North America, Oceania; organizations in countries under comprehensive U.S. OFAC sanctions ineligible.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: The call is global and open to nonprofits and research institutions; the FAQ says international/multilateral organizations (e.g., UN agencies, development banks) are 'welcome as additional partners' but cannot replace the city partner. It does not explicitly say whether an intergovernmental-type research organization such as CIAT can be lead grantee; CIAT/Bioversity are non-profit, so lead looks plausible but should be confirmed with citiesdeliver@rockfound.org (revised FAQs promised 4 Nov 2026). Alternatively CIAT can partner with an eligible local nonprofit/university lead.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Eligible organization acts as sole grantee of record; must hold a city government letter of intent; project must have a charitable purpose benefiting underserved communities; outputs must be openly licensed and published.
opportunities.geographic_restrictions: City-level (not state/national) government partners only; OFAC-sanctioned countries excluded.
opportunities.consortium_details: Joint projects allowed with one lead applicant as sole grantee; city government partner mandatory.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Develop, pilot or expand AI solutions in real city services in four areas: Public Health, Economic Mobility, Environmental Resilience ('Solutions that help cities forecast, withstand, and recover from environmental shocks'), Civic Engagement. Research-only projects are not eligible. Staff and compute/API credits are eligible; indirect costs capped at 15%.
opportunities.required_documents: Round 1: eligibility screen, Round 1 proposal (template), documentation of legal status (501(c)(3) or international equivalency determination or fiscal sponsor), city government letter of intent, short video demonstrating the AI solution. Round 2: full proposal, personnel bios, cybersecurity form, official letter or MOU from the city.
opportunities.application_procedure: Two rounds via portal citiesdeliver.rockefellerfoundation.org: Round 1 by 29 Nov 2026; interviews January 2027; Round 2 by 1 Mar 2027.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Environmental Resilience track fits AI/EO-based early warning, urban heat/flood forecasting and peri-urban food security tools, but the call is about deploying AI in city public services rather than research; our crop-modelling strengths are secondary.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Large (up to US$2M), staff-eligible, global call open to LAC/Africa/Asia cities; fits Alliance work with municipal governments (e.g., Cali, Nairobi, Hanoi) on climate risk and food systems, but urban focus is outside core landscapes portfolio.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Team has AI/GEE/EO and climate-risk capacity, but requires an already-identified city partner letter within ~4 weeks and a working AI solution/prototype video.
opportunities.recommendation: Pursue only if a city partnership and a demonstrable AI tool already exist (e.g., climate/flood/heat or urban food-security advisory with a LAC or African city). Tight Round-1 deadline; confirm CIAT lead eligibility first.
opportunities.potential_partners: City governments (e.g., Alcaldía de Cali / Bogotá, Nairobi County), local universities, existing Alliance urban food-systems partners.
opportunities.next_action: Check revised FAQs (posted 4 Nov 2026) and email citiesdeliver@rockfound.org to confirm whether CIAT/Bioversity (international non-profit research organization) can be lead; identify city partner and secure letter of intent before 29 Nov 2026.

opportunities.title: Global Centre on Biodiversity for Climate (GCBC) Research Grant Competition 4 (RGC4) - Concept Note window (Amazon, Congo Basin, Coral Triangle)
opportunities.funder: UK Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs (Defra) - Global Centre on Biodiversity for Climate (UK ICF/ODA)
opportunities.program: GCBC Research Grant Competition 4 (RGC4): Enabling transformative change - addressing drivers of biodiversity loss in three critical regions
opportunities.deadline_text: The closing date for Concept Notes is 12:00 noon GMT on 30 November 2026.
opportunities.funding_text: Projects with a budget of between £200,000 and £1,500,000; aim to fund a mixed portfolio of up to 12 grants.
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Led by a Research Organisation. UK-registered leads must be on the UKRI eligible list; non-UK leads must demonstrate they are legally constituted, have a research remit and relevant research experience. Lead organisations from ODA-eligible countries especially welcome. Private sector can be consortium partners but not lead or receive funds for profit.
opportunities.eligible_countries: Research must focus on OECD DAC (ODA)-eligible countries within the Amazon Basin, Congo Basin and Coral Triangle; at least one implementing partner legally registered in an ODA-eligible country in a focal geography.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: FAQ: lead organisations can be based outside the UK, and 'A lead organisation may be based outside the ODA country ... in such a case at least one partner organisation must be based in the ODA-country.' CIAT (legally constituted research organization headquartered in Colombia, an ODA country with Amazon territory) or Bioversity (Italy) could lead; CIAT Colombia/Peru offices could also serve as in-region partner. International-organization status not explicitly addressed; confirm with infogcbc@gcbc.org.uk.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Research Organisation, legally constituted, research remit; capable of managing the grant budget.
opportunities.geographic_restrictions: Amazon Basin (east of the Pacific/Atlantic watershed; eastern Andean slopes included; Galapagos excluded), Congo Basin, Coral Triangle; DAC-eligible countries only (French Guiana excluded; Guyana expected to graduate 2027).
opportunities.consortium_details: Partnerships expected; at least one implementing partner registered in an ODA-eligible country in a focal geography. Organisations may join more than one concept note if projects are distinct.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Research on drivers of biodiversity loss (incl. land-use change/agricultural expansion) and transformative change linked to climate and poverty in the three regions. Budget lines include staff, travel, equipment, sub-contractors, overheads (15% cap, excluding MEL).
opportunities.required_documents: Stage 1: Concept Note with indicative budget (only 10% variance allowed vs full proposal). Stage 2 (invited): full proposal.
opportunities.application_procedure: Two-stage: Concept Note via GCBC application portal (linked from Invitation to Apply Overview) by 30 Nov 2026 12:00 GMT; shortlisted applicants invited to full proposal. Clarifying-questions deadline (30 Oct) has passed.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Land-use drivers of deforestation/biodiversity loss in the Amazon map directly onto EO/remote sensing, landscape modelling and agricultural-frontier work (e.g., cattle/cacao/coffee landscapes in Colombian/Peruvian Amazon).
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Multi-year (up to 4 yrs), staff-eligible (PI up to 100% time), up to £1.5M, Amazon focus aligned with Alliance Multifunctional Landscapes and LAC presence; CIAT HQ in an eligible ODA country.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Alliance has Amazon landscape, deforestation-free value chain and EO teams and established Colombian/Peruvian partners; concept note feasible in four weeks.
opportunities.recommendation: Strong candidate: pursue an Amazon-focused concept note (agricultural drivers of biodiversity loss, EO monitoring + transformative change pathways) with CIAT as lead or with a national partner lead.
opportunities.potential_partners: Instituto SINCHI, Universidad Nacional de Colombia (Amazonía), IIAP Peru, Fundación Gaia Amazonas, UK university partners (e.g., Lancaster, Oxford ECI), CIFOR-ICRAF.
opportunities.next_action: Download Invitation to Apply Overview and Theme Paper; email infogcbc@gcbc.org.uk to confirm CIAT eligibility as lead; draft concept note and indicative budget by 30 Nov 2026 12:00 GMT.

evidence.deadline_quote: The closing date for Concept Notes is 12:00 noon GMT on 30 November 2026.
evidence.eligibility_quote: A lead organisation may be based outside the ODA country (or countries) in which research will be conducted. However, in such a case at least one partner organisation must be based in the ODA-country.

opportunities.title: Conservation, Food & Health Foundation Grant Program - Cycle 1 2027 concept applications (window 15 Oct - 22 Dec 2026)
opportunities.funder: Conservation, Food & Health Foundation (administered by GMA Foundations, Boston)
opportunities.program: Conservation, Food & Health Foundation Grants (applied research in conservation, agriculture/food, health in developing regions)
opportunities.deadline_text: Proposal Cycle 1: Concept application deadline December 22nd; proposal invitation January 15th; proposal deadline February 15th; grant awards July 1st. Concept window October 15 - December 22.
opportunities.funding_text: No minimum or maximum; most grants expected to fall between $25,000 and $50,000 per year. One-year grants usual; two-year grants possible but rare.
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Local, regional, national, and international NGOs, nonprofits, CBOs and academic institutions; government agencies and religious organizations may be partners only. One application per organization per review cycle/calendar year.
opportunities.eligible_countries: Projects in Africa, Asia, the Caribbean, Latin America and the Middle East (preference for low- and middle-income countries); organizations in upper-income countries may apply with local partners; no post-Soviet or Balkan states.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: FAQ lists 'Local, regional, national, and international NGOs' as eligible; non-US organizations register with placeholder Tax ID. CIAT (Colombia) can apply directly for a project in LAC/Africa/Asia; local leadership is prioritized.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Organization (not individual); local leadership prioritized; one concept per cycle.
opportunities.geographic_restrictions: Developing regions listed above; no post-Soviet/Balkan states.
opportunities.consortium_details: Not required; local partners expected for organizations from upper-income countries.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Applied research in natural and health sciences, pilot projects, new initiatives, training and technical assistance. Overhead/indirect costs not funded ('Applicants are more competitive when they request only direct costs'); does not typically fund salaries of Executive Directors of US/European organizations.
opportunities.required_documents: Online concept application (portal access code 'CFHgrants'); invited full proposal by 15 Feb.
opportunities.application_procedure: Register on cfhfoundation.grantsmanagement08.com portal (non-US orgs use Tax ID 12-1234567), click APPLY, enter access code CFHgrants, submit concept between 15 Oct and 22 Dec 2026; invitations by 15 Jan 2027.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Applied agricultural/conservation science for smallholders fits; small scale suits a pilot (e.g., site-specific crop-model advisory or EO-based monitoring pilot) rather than full research programme.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Small grants (US$25-50k/yr), no overhead, mostly 1 year - limited for sustaining staff, but low effort and directly accessible to CIAT.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Well within team capabilities; short concept note.
opportunities.recommendation: Low-effort complementary option for a field pilot or local-partner capacity component (e.g., Honduras crop-modelling advisory pilot); not a primary vehicle for multi-year staff funding.
opportunities.potential_partners: National partners (e.g., DICTA/Zamorano Honduras, Colombian farmer organizations) as co-leads to reflect local leadership preference.
opportunities.next_action: Decide on a pilot idea and submit concept on the portal before 22 Dec 2026.

opportunities.title: AI4D Research & Innovation for Climate (RICH) Hub - Climate AI Innovation Expressions of Interest (scaling grants up to US$200,000, Africa)
opportunities.funder: AI4D (IDRC Canada / UK FCDO), implemented by Local Development Research Institute (LDRI) with AfriClimate AI
opportunities.program: AI for Development (AI4D) - Research and Innovation for Climate Hub (RICH)
opportunities.deadline_text: accepts Expressions of Interest on a rolling basis
opportunities.funding_text: Selected innovations may receive potential scaling grants of up to USD 200,000, plus technical and innovation support, coaching, research and piloting opportunities. 'Submitting an EOI does not guarantee selection, support, or funding.'
opportunities.eligible_applicants: African climate AI innovators, researchers, startups, organizations and solution developers with African-led or Africa-based innovations at pilot stage or beyond.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: Requires 'African-led or Africa-based innovations'. An Alliance tool developed and led from the Nairobi office (or co-led with an African partner, e.g., a national met agency) may qualify; international research centres not explicitly mentioned.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: African-led or Africa-based innovation at pilot stage or beyond.
opportunities.consortium_details: Hub favours public-interest pathways such as national meteorological agencies.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Scaling climate AI solutions (climate-smart agriculture, seasonal/extreme weather forecasting, flood forecasting, carbon-sink and deforestation monitoring, etc.).
opportunities.application_procedure: Complete the RICH Hub Climate AI Innovation Expression of Interest Form (Google Form); selected innovators contacted for support/scaling grants.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Climate AI for agriculture/forecasting in Africa matches digital advisory, EO and crop-yield forecasting work.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Useful for scaling an existing African climate-ag AI tool and linking to the AI4D network; amounts modest and staffing/duration not specified.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Requires an existing pilot-stage tool; Alliance Africa has several (e.g., climate advisory/forecast tools).
opportunities.recommendation: Submit a short EOI for an Africa-led Alliance climate-AI tool with an African co-lead (e.g., national met service) - low cost, rolling.
opportunities.potential_partners: KMD (Kenya Meteorological Department), ICPAC, AfriClimate AI, national agricultural research institutes.
opportunities.next_action: Identify an Africa-led pilot-stage tool and submit the EOI form; ask LDRI whether international research centres with African offices qualify.
